title: Planner scoping a corridor mixed-use development in COR

persona.description: Urban planner consulting on a medium-density mixed-use development along a corridor

turns.user_message: I’m an urban planner working on a mixed-use development on Gottingen Street in the COR zone. The client wants a building with ground-floor commercial and multi-unit residential above. What are the use permissions in COR — is multi-unit dwelling permitted, and what about commercial/retail uses?
What are the setback requirements in COR? I’m particularly interested in whether we can build right to the front street edge or need to step back.
Is the height in COR governed by a fixed table limit or by Schedule 15? And does the same Schedule 17 FAR overlay apply in COR as it does in the other centre zones?
What is the maximum lot coverage in COR, and how does that compare to the adjacent CEN-1 zone?
For a 30-unit residential component of the building, what’s the parking requirement? Does COR benefit from the no-parking exemption, or is a parking structure required?

spec.notes: Five-turn planner scenario. Tests COR front setback (3 m, unlike CEN-1/CEN-2 at 0 m) and that COR does NOT get the no-parking exemption (Section 120(b) lists only CEN-1, CEN-2, DH, DD). High liability: full mixed-use building program.
